description:
FILED s470bq (Opus, 2026-09-05).  PRE-EXISTING and LATENT; found because it is
the ONE unexplained residue of the flag-day's 111-file A/B.

`Pl::Parser2::_forward_global_decls` finds a section's undeclared package
globals by SCANNING the assembled emission text, and `_blank_string_innards`
is what makes that safe: it blanks the contents of every string literal so a
name inside one is not read as a variable reference.  It is a character state
machine over `"` / `|â¦|` / `#\c` / `;` comments.

MEASURED, on the s470bq BASE emission (027ba9c) of `perl-tests/sort.t`:

    perl -I. -e 'require Pl::Parser2;
      open my $h,"<:raw",$f; local $/; my $t=<$h>;
      my $b = Pl::Parser2::_blank_string_innards($t);
      print scalar(() = $b =~ /\@result/g), "\n"'

answers 2 â i.e. `@result`, which occurs ONLY inside two `(p-eval "â¦")`
argument strings, SURVIVES the blanker.  The state machine believes it is
OUTSIDE a string there (traced: a bogus "open" at offset 50901 makes the real
opening quote at 50963 read as a CLOSE), and it even applied its `;`-comment
rule to the perl source inside the string.  The consequence in the emission is
a SPURIOUS `(p-defcell @result â¦)` â a package-global declaration for a name
that is lexical inside an eval'd string and is never a global at all.

WHY s470bq SURFACED IT: `p-esc` (#1212) removed the RAW NEWLINES from those
literals, which moved where the parity error lands; the same file now blanks
both occurrences and emits no `@result` cell.  **The lost cell is
behaviourally neutral â `perl sweep-perl-tests.pl --jobs 1 perl-tests/sort.t`
reads 182 pass / 6 fail / 205 planned, exactly the blessed baseline** â so
this is a latent scan bug that happened to be defused for one file, NOT a
regression.  It is the one file of 111 that the flag-day's mechanical
explanation could not attribute to p-esc, the regex literals or `:needs`.

WHY IT MATTERS: inventing a cell is the quiet half.  The same
desynchronisation can make the scanner read CODE as string content and MISS a
genuine undeclared global, which is an unbound symbol at LOAD.  And the
standing note "a dead global declaration is NOT emission-neutral" says several
sites read "has a cell" as "is a global".

WHAT TO DO: find the FIRST bad toggle (bisect the offsets where `in_str` flips
in the sort.t base text â the scanner is 30 lines, so the trigger is one
character class it gets wrong; the suspects are an escaped closing quote at
the end of a literal, a `|â¦|` symbol inside a string, and `#\` followed by a
quote).  Then decide whether this should be a TEXT scan at all:
`_forward_global_decls` is the last consumer that re-reads the assembled text,
and the structural answer is to collect the free names from the TREES the
assembly already has â which is also what task #1217 wants for the data form.
Bar: corpus-diff (no defcell list moves without a named cause) plus the FULL
sweep, because a missed global is a load failure, not a wrong answer.
subject: _blank_string_innards goes OUT OF PARITY on the emitted text, so the undeclared-global scan can read an eval STRING's contents as code (found by the s470bq flag-day, which defused one instance)
